key_insight: The paper introduces trapdoored Clifford distributions that look random to outsiders but can be sampled and implemented much faster by someone holding a trapdoor.
engineering_relevance: This could speed up quantum benchmarking, shadow tomography, and authentication workflows while also enabling more efficient classical simulation and low-depth Clifford implementations.
method: Construct a trapdoored Clifford family under a variant of the learning parity with noise assumption.
Design fast tableau action on Pauli labels for efficient classical simulation.
Build trapdoored finite-field matrices with efficient forward and inverse multiplication, then use them for Clifford synthesis and batching hardness results.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-linear-time sampling/implementation, polylogarithmic-depth optimizations, and new worst-case-to-average-case reductions for matrix and Clifford problems.
watch_item: Security and performance gains rely on a cryptographic assumption and may be sensitive to constant factors, approximation settings, and the overhead of realizing the trapdoor in practice.
